name: Trisannabrücke
kurzbeschreibung: The Trisannabrücke is at 120 m the highest railway bridge on the Arlbergbahn and offers a spectacular view into the valley.
preis: Kostenlos frei zugänglich (Parkplatz an der B188 gebührenfrei)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Trisanna Bridge (Trisannabrücke) and adjacent Schloss Wiesberg compose one of the most breathtaking and celebrated unions of historic railway engineering and medieval fortress architecture in the European Alps. Straddling the defile at the threshold of the Paznaun Valley between Strengen, Tobadill, and Pians, this colossal steel arch viaduct carries the legendary Arlberg Railway across the plunging Trisanna gorge at a dizzying height of 87 meters, spanning 120 meters unsupported. Upon its grand inauguration in 1884, it reigned as the longest-span railway bridge on the planet—a monumental triumph of imperial Austrian engineering. Perched directly beside the bridgehead on a sheer rocky promontory stands Schloss Wiesberg, a 13th-century stronghold complete with a crenellated keep and baroque chapel that guarded access to the Paznaun for centuries. Below the viaduct, the turbulent torrents of the Trisanna and Rosanna merge to birth the Sanna River, providing a dramatic spectacle of raw alpine hydrology.

Route & Requirements

Experiencing the Trisanna Bridge and Schloss Wiesberg serves equally well as a brief scenic overlook or a rewarding valley and gorge ramble. A beloved walking circuit departs from Pians or Tobadill: following shaded pine paths and farm lanes, walkers descend into the dramatic canyon to witness the river confluence before climbing along secured stone switchbacks toward panoramic viewing promontories facing the castle (distance approx. 4 km, 150 vertical meters gain/loss, walking time 1.5 hours, moderate grade T1/T2, suitable for surefooted youngsters). The opposite valley terrace provides the signature vantage point to photograph high-speed ÖBB Railjet trains gliding effortlessly across the slender steel arc high above the chasm. While Schloss Wiesberg is privately owned and closed to interior tours, the exterior approaches and viewing terraces are freely accessible. Sturdy shoes with lugged soles are advised for gorge descents. Leashed dogs are permitted on all valley footpaths.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel via ÖBB mainline trains into Landeck-Zams or St. Anton am Arlberg. From Landeck station forecourt, regional VVT bus 260 heading toward Ischgl/Galtür stops directly at "Schloss Wiesberg / Abzw. Tobadill". Motorists take the Arlberg expressway S16 (exit Pians/Paznaun) and follow the Silvretta federal highway B188. Free designated viewing laybys and trail parking are situated along the roadside beside the bridge overlook. The viewpoint is accessible year-round free of charge.

Tips

Check the train timetable or wait a few minutes at the roadside belvedere to photograph a sleek red ÖBB Railjet express crossing the soaring viaduct with the medieval castle towers framed dramatically behind it. Stop at a rustic guesthouse in nearby Pians to savor pan-seared river trout caught freshly from the alpine currents of the Sanna.
